strengths: Jointly selecting pipeline partitions and per-layer DP, TP, and FSDP strategies addresses a useful training-infrastructure problem with direct relevance to large vision models. Appendix E provides an interpretable example of adapting these choices to communication topology and memory limits.

Table 2 reports meaningful measured gains. On EnvB, ViT-Huge improves from the strongest baseline's 38.74 to 45.58 samples/s, and Swin-Huge improves from 13.90 to 19.08 samples/s. UniAP also trains Swin-Huge on EnvA where Galvatron encounters OOM.

The reported strategy-search times are substantially shorter: approximately 1.34–17.29 times faster than Galvatron across the evaluated configurations. Faster planning remains useful even on configurations where training throughput matches Galvatron.

The evaluation covers five Transformer models, including two vision architectures, and several hardware configurations. The reported 3.59% average throughput-estimation error supports the cost model's practical usefulness on the selected strategies. Hardware descriptions, model configurations, pseudocode, and solver settings provide useful reproducibility information.
weaknesses: The central formulation does not enforce valid pipeline ordering as written. Equations (6a–6c) ensure contiguity, but for a two-layer chain u→v they permit placing u in stage 2 and v in stage 1. Equation (4) then charges zero communication for that edge, potentially making this invalid ordering preferable. Appendix A proves contiguity rather than stage precedence. This affects the optimization objective and selected solution, making it a substantive correctness concern.

The claimed MIQP formulation is incomplete. Equations (3) and (4) contain products of four decision variables, such as P_ui P_vi S_uk S_vl, and therefore are not quadratic as presented. An auxiliary-variable reformulation is possible, but the manuscript does not specify the transformation or complete constraints passed to Gurobi. Consequently, the correspondence between the published formulation and the evaluated implementation cannot be verified.

The optimality and complexity claims exceed the evidence. Appendix D imposes a 60-second time limit and permits termination after 15 seconds with an optimality gap below 4%, but achieved gaps and timeout frequencies are unreported. Even an exact solution would optimize an approximate cost model within the enumerated strategy space. Treating solver runtime as a capped constant in Section 3.5 does not establish the complexity of obtaining an optimal solution.

The experiments do not isolate the contribution of joint optimization over hierarchical optimization. Figure 7 compares joint search against inter-layer-only and intra-layer-only variants, rather than a hierarchical optimizer using the same cost model and candidate strategies. Because UniAP also reports better cost estimation, the throughput gains cannot be attributed specifically to unification. Likewise, describing prior methods as hierarchical does not by itself establish their suboptimality or strict search-space containment.

Memory feasibility needs a clearer derivation. Section 3.2 scales activation memory by batch size, while Algorithm 1 passes micro-batch size b=B/c into CalculateCost. GPipe retains activations from multiple micro-batches before backward execution, yet the formulation does not show how this accumulation enters the memory constraint. This ambiguity matters because avoiding OOM is an explicit claim.

The search-time results measure UOP and omit the preceding profiling phase. Section 4.1 also attributes substantial acceleration to multithreaded Gurobi versus single-threaded baselines, without a controlled resource comparison. These results demonstrate useful implementation-level speedups, but do not establish the full preparation-time advantage or an intrinsic algorithmic speedup. Overall, the unresolved formulation correctness and insufficient validation of the central optimization claims outweigh the promising measured gains and determine the weak-reject recommendation.
